title: Consul Service Discovery
description: Configure Consul for service discovery with health checks.

data.text: HashiCorp Consul is a popular service mesh solution providing service discovery, health checking, and key-value storage. It supports both HTTP and DNS interfaces.

terms.definition: A service mesh solution by HashiCorp.
A daemon running on each node that handles registration and health checks.
The central registry of services and nodes.
A key-value store for configuration and coordination.

items: Consul agents run on each node
Agents register services and run health checks
Clients query via HTTP or DNS

data.text: Services register with Consul using the HTTP API, configuration files, or the agent CLI. Registration includes the service name, address, port, and health check.

items: TTL checks: service must renew periodically

data.text: Consul provides a DNS interface. Querying catalog.service.consul returns the IPs of healthy instances.

data.caption: Consul Architecture
data.definition:

    S -->|Catalog| DB[(Raft Store)]

items.question: Is Consul free?
items.answer: Consul has a free open-source version and paid enterprise features.

items.question: Consul vs Eureka?
items.answer: Consul offers more features (KV store, multi-datacenter) but is more complex. Eureka is simpler and Spring-native.

items.question: How does Consul handle multi-datacenter?
items.answer: Consul replicates the catalog across datacenters with WAN gossip.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Consul provides discovery, health checks, and KV store
data.takeaway: Consul is a full-featured service mesh with discovery and health checks.
